Actual Article Body:
Donald Trump and the Republicans struggle to spin a historic defeat in the US midterms.

It was the most expensive election in American history: nearly $12bn spent, much of it on advertisements, with the majority of that money going to Republican candidates. But most voters weren’t buying it. The result: a Democratic sweep on a scale not seen in half a century.

In the aftermath of the vote, United States President Donald Trump – who has long revelled in his ability to turn controversy and crisis into spectacle – appeared to lose control of the narrative. The scale of the Republican defeat amounts to a repudiation of Trump’s politics and the US-Israel war on Iran. Meenakshi Ravi and Richard Gizbert examine the political and media fallout.

Contributors: 
Alex Shephard – Senior editor, The New Republic
Rob Arlett – former Trump state campaign chair & Republican strategist
Maya Berry – Executive director, Arab American Institute

A federal judge Thursday barred the Trump administration from pressuring Washington election officials to set aside ballots cast by voters the Department of Justice (DOJ) has accused of being noncitizens, delivering another blow to the administration’s efforts to intervene in the 2026 midterms.

U.S. District Judge Jamal Whitehead issued a 14-day temporary restraining order prohibiting DOJ and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) from demanding that Washington officials remove registered voters from the rolls, refuse to issue them ballots or segregate and withhold their votes from the count. The order also bars federal officials from threatening election workers with prosecution for refusing to comply.

The US Secret Service arrested a man near the White House Thursday who allegedly had several guns in a stolen car and was threatening to kill President Donald Trump.

According to the Department of Homeland Security, Secret Service agents noticed Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos – a Venezuela national who DHS said entered the US illegally – acting suspiciously in a car along side the White House.

“When they confronted the suspect, he said that he heard voices in his head telling him to come to Washington, D.C. and kill President Trump,” DHS said in a news release. “The officers then discovered that the vehicle had been reported stolen, and the suspect admitted to having weapons in his vehicle.”

The agents discovered a rifle and two handguns along with dozens of rounds of ammunition in the car, DHS said.
